questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to travel further than Europe and explore new cultures and universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find all the information through Westerns website. But when you get accepted to the university you will start getting emails upon arrival that helps with practical stuff like how to get housing, what should you pack and how do you register for courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The only assistance i got was through email and i was mostly about UNI stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
The first week was intro-week for International and Exchange students it was great but mostly information, the socializing part was mostly up to yourself. They don't have games and stuff for students to get to know each other.

The second week was O-week an intro-week for the first year students. This is also something you can attend, but you have to pay for it. It has more events like shows and a concert, but still you have to kind of just talk to people you meet on the go.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, we were a group of 5 danish students that found a house off campus through AirBnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Living off campus is fine in London Ontario, because you automatically have a free bus card through your student card and the buses drives every 15-30 minutes. If you want to make a lot of international friends this is easier living on campus, otherwise get some friends that lives on-campus that can invite you into the residencies.
In downtown London students go partying and living off-campus might actually be closer to downtown than living on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very difficult to figure out exactly how to apply for courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was very difficult to figure out exactly how to apply for courses. First you had to visit
student.uwo.ca
where you had to apply for courses. Remember to also use another application called Draft A Shedule and chech if you're different courses can be taken together. Courses called a number and B (like 4355B) is in the spring while courses in ending on A is in autumn semester. There are also other codes like C, D, E and F but i dont remember exactly what they were.
After applying on the first website you have to send a mail and tell them exactly what you applied fore. Usually you will end up having to change some of your courses but you can do that until 1 or 2 weeks into the semester start, so dont stress.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
You could write to goabroad@
uwo.ca
which was very helpfull and wrote back within some minutes usually.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3 out of 4 courses i applied for and ended up changing one course in the beginning of my semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Try to apply as soon as you get accepted to the university, and browse a bit around the website
student.uwo.ca
and check your email frequently.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took courses in level 1000, level 2000, level 3000 and level 4000.
I would definitely recommend taking courses 2000 or above. Level 1000 courses are very basic and usually has a lot of reading and boring mandatory extra stuff because it is for first year students that has to learn how to attend university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PSYCHOL 1002A - Psychology as a Natural Science (do not recommend, it is a methodical course with lots of basic reading and a lot of mandatory attending)
MICROIMM 2500A - Microbiology and Immunology (basic course in immune system, bacteriology, virology and other infectious agents - only thing is that it has 2 midterms and one exam)
BIOLOGY 3592A - Principles of Human Genetics (good course)
BIOLOGY 4355F - The Biology of Aging (best course i ever had!)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIOLOGY 4355F - The Biology of Aging (best course i ever had!) 
The professor Dr. Robert Cumming is a really great teacher and it has some very interesting lectures with lots of papers. Theres no reading in the course, only in one small asignment.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: UHIP is a mandatory health insurance which costs around 1500.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive in Canada also buying groceries in the supermarked, so if you can try to make big meals or make food with others and share the cost.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
You can what all games on campus for free :) including ishockey matches and football games.
I did not join any clubs because i went traveling a lot so it did not make sense for me to join a club and spend time there. But there are plenty of choices if you're interested in clubs!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The recreation center (træningscentret) is free for students and very nice!
Also all games on campus are free :)
Other activities:
- Homecoming (HOCO) here you should wear purple ;)
- Global cafe on every thursday

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Watch some of the games on campus like the first football match in O-week and attend HOCO.
Explore London city and do different activities like escape rooms, iceskating, hockeygames, christmas markets, dinning and concerts.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- Banff National Park
- Montreal
- Vancouver 
- Niagara falls
- New York
- Apple farms in London Ontario
- Watch an ishockey game with London Knights
- Toronto

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general it was easy to adapt to the culture. But be aware of taxes (13%) and tips (around 10-20%) each time you buy something. Also if you live off campus groceries shopping can be difficult because you have to either walk far (compared to copenhagen) or have a car.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out partying in downtown and do events. Living on-campus makes it a bit easier to socialize with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Remembering to calculate taxes and tips when trying to figure out what things would cost

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
People are asy to talk to and the older people are nice in Canada. 
Our neighbours an elderly couple were the best you could ever wish for and invited us over for christmas dinner.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- try to make plans ahead if you wanna travel
- get use to checking your different courses for mandatory quizzes and tests
- getting Canadians friends is very difficult, while exchange students are usually more open to meeting new people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
- it is nice to live close to a supermarked, if not you should consider having a car
- Ubers are lifesavers when getting home drunk...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience a different culture. I though Canada would be somewhat similar to Denmark, but actually i ended up being very suprissed about how different it felt. It was a great experience and i had a lot of fun traveling and living with friends and meeting other exchange students. A great tip is to go traveling somewhere else like South America after your courses are done in the end of december!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to figure out another university system and getting use to having more free time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have a great stay and remember to take some photos because you will forget a lot of the things you experience if you dont have pictures or other kinds of reminders.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
